enforcement_scripts_note: The scripts that actually enforce containment are pinned here because the governed inventory only walks governance/ and release/, so tools/ carries no hash of its own. This record IS in governed_artifacts, so editing an enforcement script without updating this map fails tests/test_v2f_containment_mutations.py, and updating this map changes the record's hash and so fails `fable5 verify` until the inventory is rebuilt. Neither half is a self-hash: each is pinned by the other.
mutual_pinning_limitation: Read enforcement_scripts_note for what the digest chain does, and this for what it does NOT do. The chain detects DRIFT, not FORGERY. Executed on 2026-07-29 in a disposable clone: forging active=false with a lifted_by and lifted_on opens the gate (exit 0); `fable5 verify` then reports byte drift plus surface_digest drift; but `fable5 build --write` followed by `freeze-build --write` — two committed, legitimate CLI commands — makes BOTH verifiers report ok:true over the forgery, and all 34 tests in tests/test_v2f_containment_mutations.py pass against the laundered tree. The controls that actually caught it are hard-coded live-state assertions in tests/test_v2f_containment_gate.py and tests/test_v2f_research_partition_determination.py (5 failures across the two, both CI-enforced on every push). Anyone relying on the digest chain alone to detect a forged lift is relying on something two commands turn green.

suspended_workflow_note: The PRIMARY control on the suspended workflow is this whole-file digest, not the structural checks in tests/test_m3e_workflow_security.py. Those checks scan text; a read-only auditor broke four of them with valid YAML that GitHub honours - a cron placed AFTER workflow_dispatch (the trigger test was substring containment, not the exact match its comment claimed), a job header carrying a trailing space or comment (invisible to the job regex), steps indented eight spaces instead of six (parsed as zero steps, hiding an inert gate), and a job with no checkout that curls directly. PyYAML is deliberately not a dependency, so a hand-written parser would only relocate those blind spots: the checker cannot see YAML semantics, and it can never see runtime behaviour at all (PATH, working-directory, what a `uses:` does). A digest has no parser and no blind spot. While containment is active the workflow is suspended and must not change AT ALL, so any edit - however spelled - fails this pin and must be argued for in a governance diff a human reads. The structural checks are retained, and fixed, as a secondary explanatory control for the day containment is lifted and the file legitimately changes.
